summary: Minimum total x added over subarray-increment operations so the array becomes non-decreasing.
mainInsight: Only descents matter. At each i with nums[i] > nums[i+1], the suffix starting at i+1 must be raised by at least the drop; operations on suffixes are free to combine, so the answer is the sum of all positive drops max(0, nums[i] - nums[i+1]).

cards.answer: The sum of every positive drop nums[i] - nums[i+1]
cards.explanation: Each descent forces the suffix after it up by exactly the drop.

promptVariants: Why can each drop be fixed independently, with the suffix after it raised by the drop?
Why is the sum of drops also a lower bound?
cards.answer: Raising the suffix starting at i + 1 by d closes the drop at i without changing any other adjacent difference, so the drops are independent. Each positive drop must be closed by increments that start exactly at i + 1 (an operation starting later or earlier cannot change that adjacent difference by itself), so the total of x values is at least the sum of the drops.
keyPoints: Sum of drops is also a lower bound
cards.explanation: Increments must start exactly at i + 1 to change only that difference.
